newsitem.title: USA: Barr Labs sees FDA anti-coagulant approval.
newsitem.headline: Barr Labs sees FDA anti-coagulant approval.

text.p: Barr Laboratories Inc said on Tuesday it expected its application to market Warfarin Sodium tablets, a generic version of an anti-coagulant, to be approved soon.
Warfarin was a generic version of an anti-coagulant made by the DuPont Merck joint venture.
Barr said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration had completed its pre-approval inspection of the product.
Barr said DuPont Merck was trying to delay the approval of its generic drug, by asking the FDA to change the bioequivalence guidelines for the product.

"Barr intends to fight all attempts to deny hundreds of thousands of patients with heart disease the opportunity to purchase an equivalent generic at a fair price," Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Bruce Downey said in a statement.
DuPont Merck was not immediately available for comment.
If the drug was approved, Barr said it would be the only generic supplier of this therapy.
